definition: I. [ סָלַל ] verb lift up, cast up (Late Hebrew סִלְסֵל esteem highly , סִלְסוּל loftiness, distinction ; סוּלָּם ladder; ᵑ7 סוּלְּמָא id. ; MI 26 מסלת highway ; Phoenician סלמת stair (?) Lzb 329 ; Assyrian sellu , sillu , perhaps breast-works Dl HWB 501 ; Arabic is draw out, forth Lane 1395 = שָׁלַל , but ladder (a loan-word according to Schw ZMG liii (1899), 197 ), compare סֻלָּם ; see also ‰rry , siege-wall , Egyptian loan-word from סֹלְלָה according to WMM As.u.Eur.101 ); — Qal Imperfect וַיָּסֹ֫לּוּ Job 19:12 ; Job 30:12 Imperative masculine plural סֹ֫לּוּ Isa 57:14 + 4 t.; suffix סָלּוּהָ Jer 50:26 (compare סֶ֫לָה ); Passive participle סְלוּלָה Jer 18:15 סְלֻלָה Prov 15:19 — 1. cast up a highway: מְסִלָּה ׳ ס Isa 62:10 (twice in verse), without object Isa 57:14 (twice in verse), דֶּרֶךְ לֹא סְלוּלָה Jer 18:15 figurative of path of upright Prov 15:19 . 2. cast up a way: דֶּרֶךְ with על against , Job 19:12 (of besieger, in figure), ארה Job 30:12 (of besetting foe); Babylonian as a heap of garbage Jer 50:26 . 3. lift up (a song) Ps 68:5 , with לְ person (|| שׁיר , זמּר ; most as 1. ). Pilpel Imperative suffix סַלְסְלֶהָ Prov 4:8 exalt her (i.e. Wisdom), i.e. (compare Toy) esteem highly, prize. Hithpa`el Participle מִסְתּוֺלֵל Exod 9:17 ( J ) exalt oneself , with בְּ against (denominative from סֹלְלָה according to Gerber 52 ); compare Eccl 39:24 ; Eccl 40:28 .
